data.why: A nuclear plant hall cut open beside a river with a small boat and the town on the far bank; the story follows the energy from the uranium in the tank to the steam, the turbine, the river water, the cooling tower and the power lines to the town. Each problem is seen on the thing (red-hot rods, boiling water, steam stalling the turbine, steam over the river round the boat, the dark town), and it ends sealing the hook's reactor in its dome as the town lights up.

story.title: How a nuclear power plant works

surprises.claim: Control rods absorb neutrons and slow down the chain reaction in a nuclear reactor.

surprises.claim: A nuclear plant's heat boils water into steam that spins a turbine connected to a generator.

surprises.claim: Cooling towers release heat as water vapor, and their white plume is not smoke.
surprises.search: cooling tower plume water vapor not smoke nuclear

surprises.claim: A thick concrete containment structure surrounds the reactor to keep radiation in.

sentences.text: If you put uranium rods in water, you have a reactor.
But the rods heat up until the core glows red.
So control rods slide in and slow it.
But even slowed, the core boils the water.
So the steam spins a turbine and generator.
But used steam piles up and stalls the turbine.
So cold river water turns it back to water.
But the warm water steams over the river.
So a cooling tower vents the heat as a cloud.
But past the tower, the town stays dark.
So power lines carry it across the river.
This is a nuclear power plant.
Seal the reactor in a dome, and the town lights up.
